category_info.edible_part: fruit (botanically a berry, eaten as a vegetable)
category_info.planting_season: sow indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost; transplant after soil reaches 15°C
category_info.harvest_window: pick when fully colored and slightly soft; twist off with the calyx for longer storage
category_info.watering_need: 2.5-5 cm of water per week, consistently moist but never waterlogged

observations.symptom: Concentric brown target-like spots with yellow halo
observations.evidence: Multiple 3-5 mm necrotic lesions visible on the leaf surface

observations.location: Leaf margins around the necrotic lesions
observations.evidence: Discoloration spreading outward from the lesions toward the leaf edge

possible_causes.name: Early Blight (Alternaria solani)
possible_causes.reason: Concentric ring lesions on lower leaves are characteristic of early blight fungal infection

possible_causes.name: Septoria Leaf Spot
possible_causes.reason: Smaller circular spots are also common in warm humid conditions

recommended_actions.action: Prune and safely discard heavily spotted lower leaves (do not compost)
recommended_actions.reason: Stops fungal spores from splashing up onto healthy upper foliage

recommended_actions.action: Water strictly at the soil base in the morning, keeping leaves dry
recommended_actions.reason: Reduces the prolonged leaf moisture required for fungal spore germination

recommended_actions.action: Ensure adequate spacing between plants for air circulation
recommended_actions.reason: Helps foliage dry quickly after morning dew or rain

seasonal_context: Warm, humid mid-summer conditions frequently trigger fungal leaf spots in nightshades.
what_to_monitor: Whether new spots appear on higher leaves or fruit stems
Neighboring plants for similar leaf spotting
limitations: A single leaf photo cannot inspect root health, soil moisture, or stem lesions
Microscopic spore analysis is needed for definitive fungal species confirmation
follow_up_questions: Are spots also visible on the stems or green fruit?
Has the plant had heavy overhead watering or frequent rain recently?
